_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_as_of:
2026-08-23 · Session 185 (SkyScope) worked the queue. Sierra went dark again overnight — the Anthropic balance ran out for the second time in two days, and for the second time nobody was told; a session happened to look. Sam topped it up and she is back. The rest of the run: a cheap monitor so the third time is caught in hours rather than by luck, prompt caching so the bill stops paying full price for the same 3,200 tokens every turn, a smoke-test assertion that had been red on correct answers since Session 125, and MAP's sandbox colleges removed from the data Sierra reads.

2026-08-23 · SkyBound (Session 184) finished the funding model with two changes. A maximum allocation now sits beside the minimum, editable, at $400,000 — but measuring it first changed the story: it holds two colleges and moves about a third of a percent, because a college already pinned to the minimum cannot be lifted by a maximum. Then the rural allowance came out and the minimum went up to $175,000 in its place, which pays those 13 colleges $236,406 more than the allowance ever did. Ten of the 13 would not have moved a dollar without the raise, and three would have gone backwards. Separately: Sierra is down on a billing balance, and your noncredit question now has numbers under it — noncredit turns out to be 111 institutions, not four.
_status:
Sierra is answering again. The thing worth knowing is that BOTH outages were found by accident: nothing watches her, because the only two test workflows run when someone presses a button. There is now an automatic check every three hours that raises a GitHub issue the moment she stops answering and closes it when she recovers. It is set to three hours rather than hourly on purpose — you are paying for this personally right now, and hourly would be about $22 a month against $7. Raise it once billing moves to the corporate account; the cost math is written into the file so it is a decision, not a guess.

On your Haiku question: there is no Haiku 4.6 — the current one is Haiku 4.5, and it is 3x cheaper than the Sonnet she runs on today. But the bigger and safer saving was that she used NO prompt caching at all, so about 3,200 tokens of identical instructions were billed at full price on every single question. That is now cached. Haiku is still worth trying afterwards, and we have the test suite to score it honestly rather than guess.

Separately, on the funding model: The funding model is where you left it plus one dial fewer. Two bounds, both editable in one box: a $175,000 minimum and a $400,000 maximum. The rural allowance is gone from every screen, the CSV and the college rows; the rural flag itself stays in the data because it is a true fact about those colleges, it just no longer moves money. Three things want you rather than a session. The pair of numbers is your call and the alternative you floated — hold the minimum at $150,000 and send the freed million to noncredit — is costed and ready either way. The noncredit question has an answer now, and it is bigger than expected: 111 institutions carry noncredit, so the floor you named only fits if the roster is scoped, and a 500-FTES cut-off fits inside the existing million. And Sierra is returning errors on an empty Anthropic balance, which nothing alerts on. Nothing else is blocked; the model is correct at any setting of the dials.

items.text: Move Sierra's Anthropic billing to the corporate account when you can. She went dark twice in two days on the personal balance — 2026-08-21 and again overnight — and each outage takes down every place she appears at once: the public page, the COBI tab, the Fact Sheet drawer, map.rccd.edu, the college landing pages and the vendor iframe. A student who arrives in that window gets nothing and files no complaint, so the outage cannot report itself. There is now an automatic check every three hours that will open a GitHub issue and close it on recovery, so you will hear about the next one — but it tells you after the fact, it does not prevent it.

Deploy the prompt-caching change and confirm it is actually caching. The code is merged but inert until cpl-chat is redeployed from the workflow. After deploying, run the smoke suite and read the function log for the new 'cpl-chat cache: read=… write=…' line — if both numbers stay at zero, something is invalidating the cached block every turn and the change is costing MORE than before, not less. Note this deploy also reorders the prompt (the always-on rules now come before the retrieved sources, because caching only works on the front of a prompt), so the smoke suite is the real gate, not the unit tests.

Trial Haiku 4.5 against the smoke suite once caching is live. It is a third of Sonnet's price both directions. Two things to check rather than assume: her context window drops from 1M to 200K, and the caveats are the product — a smaller model drops a hedge before it drops a fact, and several of the 21 smoke assertions test exactly those hedges. Run it, diff the failures, and report rather than switching quietly.

The College Identity tab was reporting 'Nothing outstanding' while ten real findings existed. Its finding list is built from an optional input, and a rebuild on 2026-08-21 ran without it: the list went from 13 to zero in a diff that looked like tidying, and stayed empty through four merges. It is restored, and the builder now refuses to publish an unchecked list over a checked one. Worth a look — two of the ten are the trailing-space college names that were making real CPL contacts invisible.

Pick the floor and ceiling pair. Live right now: a $175,000 minimum and a $400,000 maximum, both editable side by side in the Funding pools box. What that pair actually does: 69 of the 115 colleges land on the minimum — the middle college in the state is now funded by the minimum rather than by its size — and the maximum holds only two colleges and moves $82,815, about a third of one percent. So the minimum is doing nearly all the work and the maximum is close to decoration at this level. The cost is real and worth seeing before you settle: a floor is paid for by the colleges above it, so a mid-sized college now earns $4,419 per CPL FTES against the $5,650 statewide rate — 78 cents on the dollar. The alternative you floated is still open and still costed: hold the minimum at $150,000 and send the freed $1,000,000 to noncredit instead. Both are the same change with two different dial settings.

Decide how wide the noncredit lane should be. You asked what a $25,000 floor and $100,000 ceiling would look like for our other noncredit institutions, and the first number reframes the question: noncredit is not four institutions, it is 111. One hundred and eight of the 115 credit colleges already carry noncredit FTES, alongside the three standalone continuing-education institutions. At that width the numbers you named do not fit — 111 floors of $25,000 is $2,775,000, nearly three times the $1,000,000 carve-out, and still short even if the retired rural million is added on top. At exactly that figure everyone sits on the floor and the FTES basis does nothing at all. The lever is the roster, not the bounds: institutions with 500 or more noncredit FTES are 33 of them and carry 87 percent of the lane, and they fit inside the existing $1,000,000 — 27 at the $25,000 floor, the largest at $89,586, the ceiling never binding. Two cautions. Mt. SAC's noncredit FTES is currently counted twice in our data, which is harmless today and wrong the day noncredit money follows that number. And 'only what came from the noncredit landing pages' is a rule the data feed cannot tell apart yet — sizing the pool is the easy half.

Read 'How this funding model works' end to end in a browser before you send it to anyone. It is the audience-facing walk-through for the Chancellor's Office and possibly Finance, and the link now sits at the top right of the Implementation Funding title row. It has been rebuilt twice since you last saw it: the maximum is in it, the rural allowance is out of it, and the minimum is $175,000 — so the opening figures, the count of colleges at the minimum (69 now, was 45) and the worked example have all changed. The worked example is Long Beach, because the two largest colleges are now pinned to a round number their own share does not explain. No session can look at it; the sandbox cannot reach the site. One footnote: if you are still commenting on an older copy of this page, those comments do not reach the version the tab links to — comment on the linked one, and tell us when you have, because nothing pings us automatically.

MAP needs to give us two college IDs. You ruled that Calbright and LAUNCH each have two entities — one credit, one noncredit. The noncredit halves already have IDs; the credit halves ("Calbright College Credit" and "Launch Apprenticeship Non-Credit") have none anywhere we can see, and MAP is the only system allowed to assign one. We deliberately did NOT make one up, because a fake ID would look exactly like a real one to every other system. They show as "awaiting MAP ID" on the College Identity tab. Once MAP supplies them, they fold in with no code change.
Twelve credentials are marked statewide in the adoption file but are missing from Sierra's catalog entirely, so she cannot find them at all. Carried from an earlier session and still open.

Please open the three public pages on your phone — the Fact Sheet, Sierra, and the Veteran Sprint map. This is the last thing no session can check: we are blocked from reaching the live site, so all of it is verified in a test browser only. On the Fact Sheet, scroll to Statewide CPL credit recommendations — each program area should sit on its own line with four labelled figures beneath it (Exhibits, Credit recs, Adoptions, Could adopt); before the fix the name printed on top of the first number and Could adopt was cut off entirely. On the Veteran map, the side panel with the college details and the two directories was being hidden completely on any phone — it should now sit below the map. On Sierra, the faint grey notes under the answer box should be readable. If anything looks cramped or odd, tell me and I will tune it.

Give Calbright Credit and Launch Non-Credit a placeholder row so they stop disappearing. They are missing from the identity table entirely, which means they silently fall out of four other tables rather than showing up as a known gap. A row with no ID and a stated reason is safe; inventing an ID is not.

Join our tables on MAP's college ID instead of the college name. Sam asked whether we are making the best use of location IDs rather than text — measured, and he is right: 13 tables carry MAP's ID, 18 do not, and the ones that do not are all the tables we build ourselves. That is why a stray space in a college name could hide a real CPL coordinator. Four colleges' contacts are currently found only through the variant list we added last week.

Have a look at the tabs now that text runs the full width. You said the short text columns look awkward against the full-width tables, so every paragraph across 17 files now runs to the same right edge as the tables beside it. Nobody has seen it rendered. If it reads too wide, two columns is the alternative and it is a single switch, not a rebuild.
